question.text: Mr. Vikram Pillai distributes units of the Vindhya Event-Driven Fund (Cat III) to HNI clients. Under SEBI regulations, which statement about distributors of AIFs is CORRECT?

answer.text: A distributor can be empanelled with only ONE AIF at a time to avoid conflicts.
Only banks are permitted to distribute AIF units to retail investors.
Distributors are required to be SEBI-registered Portfolio Managers.
A distributor can be empanelled with MORE THAN ONE AIF, and can be an individual, distribution company, broking company, or bank.

explanation.text: The Logic: A distributor CAN be empanelled with more than one AIF. Distributors can be individuals, distribution companies, broking firms, or banks. They need proper training and thorough understanding of AIF products given the sophisticated-investor profile. They must understand risk-return and suitability and perform case-by-case client mapping. There is no PM-registration requirement for AIF distribution. The Trap: Option A invents exclusivity. Option B wrongly narrows eligible distributors. Option C conflates AIF distribution with Portfolio Manager registration. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B (Cat III Distributor) tests this directly and deeply. XIX-A (Cat I/II Distributor) tests same multi-empanelment rule. Managers only see this peripherally.
